questions.question: A chord of a circle of radius 12 cm subtends an angle of 120 degrees at the centre. Find the area of the corresponding segment of the circle. (Use pi = 3.14 and sqrt(3) = 1.73)
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exercise 11.1 Question 7

questions.subtopic: Horse Tied at Corner of Square Grass Field
questions.question: A horse is tied to a peg at one corner of a square shaped grass field of side 15 m by means of a 5 m long rope. Find the area of that part of the field in which the horse can graze. (Use pi = 3.14)
questions.explanation: At the corner of a square, angle is 90 degrees. The grazed region is a quadrant of radius 5 m. Area = (1/4) * pi * r^2 = (1/4) * 3.14 * 5^2 = (1/4) * 3.14 * 25 = 78.5 / 4 = 19.625 m^2.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exercise 11.1 Question 8(i)

questions.subtopic: Increase in Grazing Area with Longer Rope
questions.question: For the horse in Question 2, find the increase in the grazing area if the rope were 10 m long instead of 5 m. (Use pi = 3.14)
questions.explanation: With 10 m rope: Area = (1/4) * 3.14 * 10^2 = 78.5 m^2. Increase in grazing area = 78.5 - 19.625 = 58.875 m^2.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exercise 11.1 Question 8(ii)

questions.question: A circular brooch is made with silver wire in the form of a circle with diameter 35 mm. The wire is also used in making 5 diameters which divide the circle into 10 equal sectors. What is the total length of the silver wire required? (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Circumference = pi * d = (22/7) * 35 = 110 mm. Wire used in 5 diameters = 5 * 35 = 175 mm. Total wire length = 110 + 175 = 285 mm.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exercise 11.1 Question 9(i)

questions.question: For the brooch in Question 4 (diameter 35 mm, 10 equal sectors), find the area of each sector of the brooch. (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exercise 11.1 Question 9(ii)

questions.question: An umbrella has 8 ribs which are equally spaced. Assuming the umbrella to be a flat circle of radius 45 cm, find the area between two consecutive ribs of the umbrella. (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Since there are 8 equally spaced ribs, the circle is divided into 8 equal sectors. Each sector angle = 360 / 8 = 45 deg. Area = (1/8) * pi * r^2 = (1/8) * (22/7) * 45 * 45 = (11/28) * 2025 = 22275 / 28 cm^2.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exercise 11.1 Question 10

questions.subtopic: Car Dual Windshield Wipers Swept Area
questions.question: A car has two wipers which do not overlap. Each wiper has a blade of length 25 cm sweeping through an angle of 115 degrees. Find the total area cleaned at each sweep of the blades. (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exercise 11.1 Question 11

questions.question: To warn ships for underwater rocks, a lighthouse spreads a red coloured light over a sector of angle 80 degrees to a distance of 16.5 km. Find the area of the sea over which the ships are warned. (Use pi = 3.14)
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exercise 11.1 Question 12

questions.subtopic: Round Table Cover with 6 Equal Designs
questions.question: A round table cover has six equal designs as shown in the figure. If the radius of the cover is 28 cm, find the total area of the six designed segments. (Use pi = 22/7, sqrt(3) = 1.7)
questions.explanation: Each design corresponds to a segment of angle 360 / 6 = 60 degrees. Area of 1 sector = (60/360) * (22/7) * 28 * 28 = (1/6) * 22 * 4 * 28 = 2464 / 6 = 1232 / 3 cm^2. Area of 1 equilateral triangle = (sqrt(3)/4) * 28^2 = (1.7 / 4) * 784 = 1.7 * 196 = 333.2 cm^2. Area of 1 design segment = 1232/3 - 333.2 = 410.67 - 333.2 = 77.47 cm^2. Total area of 6 designs = 6 * (1232/3 - 333.2) = 2464 - 1999.2 = 464.8 cm^2.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exercise 11.1 Question 13

questions.subtopic: Cost of Round Table Cover Designs
questions.question: For the round table cover in Question 9 (area of designs = 464.8 cm^2), find the cost of making the designs at the rate of Rs 0.35 per cm^2.
questions.explanation: Cost = Area * Rate = 464.8 cm^2 * Rs 0.35 = Rs 162.68.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exercise 11.1 Question 13

questions.question: A running track has left and right ends as semicircles. The distance between the two inner parallel line segments is 60 m and they are each 106 m long. If the track is 10 m wide everywhere, what is the distance around the track along its inner edge?
questions.explanation: Inner straightaways = 2 * 106 = 212 m. Two semicircles of inner diameter 60 m form one complete circle of radius 30 m: Circumference = 2 * (22/7) * 30 = 1320 / 7 m. Total inner distance = 212 + 1320/7 = (1484 + 1320)/7 = 2804 / 7 m.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exemplar Problem

questions.question: For the running track in Question 11 (inner diameter 60 m, straightaways 106 m, track width 10 m), what is the total area of the running track?
questions.explanation: Area of 2 rectangular straightaways = 2 * (106 * 10) = 2120 m^2. The two semicircular ends form a circular ring with inner radius r = 30 m and outer radius R = 30 + 10 = 40 m. Ring area = pi * (40^2 - 30^2) = (22/7) * (1600 - 900) = (22/7) * 700 = 2200 m^2. Total track area = 2120 + 2200 = 4320 m^2.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exemplar Problem

questions.subtopic: Inscribed Square in Circle Area Ratio
questions.question: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius r. What is the ratio of the area of the circle to the area of the square?
questions.explanation: Diagonal of inscribed square = diameter of circle = 2r. Side of square s = 2r / sqrt(2) = r*sqrt(2). Area of square = s^2 = 2r^2. Area of circle = pi * r^2. Ratio of Circle Area to Square Area = (pi * r^2) / (2r^2) = pi : 2.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exemplar Problem

questions.question: A square circumscribes a circle of radius r. What is the ratio of the area of the circle to the area of the circumscribed square?
questions.explanation: Side of circumscribed square = diameter of circle = 2r. Area of square = (2r)^2 = 4r^2. Area of circle = pi*r^2. Ratio = (pi * r^2) / (4r^2) = pi : 4.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exemplar Problem

questions.subtopic: Circle Inscribed in Equilateral Triangle Area Ratio
questions.question: What is the ratio of the area of an equilateral triangle of side 'a' to the area of its incircle?
questions.explanation: Area of equilateral triangle = (sqrt(3)/4) a^2. Inradius r = a / (2*sqrt(3)). Area of incircle = pi * r^2 = pi * (a^2 / 12). Ratio = [(sqrt(3)/4) a^2] / [pi * a^2 / 12] = (sqrt(3)/4) * (12/pi) = 3*sqrt(3) / pi.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exemplar Problem

questions.question: The wheels of a car are of diameter 80 cm each. How many complete revolutions does each wheel make in 10 minutes when the car is travelling at a speed of 66 km/h? (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Speed = 66 km/h = 66 * 1000 * 100 / 60 cm/min = 110,000 cm/min. Distance in 10 mins = 1,100,000 cm. Wheel diameter = 80 cm => Circumference = pi * d = (22/7) * 80 = 1760 / 7 cm. Revolutions = 1,100,000 / (1760 / 7) = (1,100,000 * 7) / 1760 = 4375 revolutions.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exercise 11.1 Question 4

questions.question: Inside a square ABCD of side 14 cm, four semicircles are drawn with each side as diameter, intersecting to form a 4-petal flower design. What is the area of the shaded 4 petals? (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Area of square = 14^2 = 196 cm^2. Area of 4 semicircles of radius 7 cm = 4 * [(1/2) * (22/7) * 7^2] = 2 * 154 = 308 cm^2. Shaded area of overlap (petals) = Sum of areas of 4 semicircles - Area of square = 308 - 196 = 112 cm^2.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exemplar Problem

questions.question: What is the total perimeter of a sector of angle theta and radius r?
questions.explanation: A sector is bounded by the arc of length (theta/360)*2*pi*r and the two bounding radial edges (2r). Total perimeter = arc length + 2r.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Section 11.2

questions.question: The area of a sector of a circle of radius 36 cm is 54 pi cm^2. Find the length of the corresponding arc of the sector.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exemplar Problem

questions.subtopic: Percentage Area Increase from Radius Increase
questions.question: If the radius of a circle is increased by 50%, by what percentage does the area of the circle increase?
questions.explanation: New radius R = 1.5 r. New area = pi * R^2 = pi * (1.5 r)^2 = 2.25 * pi * r^2. Increase = 2.25 - 1.0 = 1.25 times the original area = 125% increase.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 11, Exemplar Problem
